title: Add repository outline and Apollo 11 1201/1202 alarm history
body:
Exploration/documentation for the repo: **`outline.markdown`** — a newcomer's guide: what the repo is (transcribed Apollo 11 AGC source), top-level structure, the CM (`Comanche055`) and LM (`Luminary099`) programs and notable files, a suggested reading order, and tooling notes. **`errorcodes.markdown`** — validated history of the 1201/1202 program alarms plus a full annotated execution trace through the actual flight code (memory-cycle timing, the radar cycle-stealing mechanism, the `READACCS`/`SERVICER`/`FINDVAC` loop, the exact `OCT 1201`/`OCT 1202` failure points, and the `BAILOUT`→`ENEMA`→phase-table restart recovery), with a `NOTE(...)` index for walking the trace in the source. **`timeline.markdown`** — second-by-second reconstruction of the five alarms during powered descent: GET/UTC/T+PDI for every event, altitudes and descent rates, verbatim air-to-ground exchanges, light-time-delay analysis of Armstrong's "Give us a reading on the 1202" → "We're Go" wait, and documented source discrepancies. **In-source annotations (`Luminary099/*.agc`)** — the alarm's execution path is annotated directly in the flight code as `NOTE(
):` comment blocks, where `
` is each module's internal `$$/…` log-section name and `` is the global execution order 1→12. Walk them via: ```bash grep -rn "NOTE(" Luminary099/*.agc ``` Order (interwoven across modules): `NOTE(ERAS1)` radar CDU counters → `NOTE(WAIT2)` `T3RUPT` clock → `NOTE(SERV3)` `READACCS` → `NOTE(SERV4)` leaking `FINDVAC` call → `NOTE(EXEC5)` `OCT 1201` → `NOTE(EXEC6)` `OCT 1202` → `NOTE(ALARM7)` `BAILOUT1` → `NOTE(ALARM8)` `WHIMPER` → `NOTE(START9)` `ENEMA` → `NOTE(START10)` queue wipe → `NOTE(RSTAB11)` `5.4SPOT` rebuild → `NOTE(SERV12)` `REREADAC` recovery. Each note links to the next, so you can follow the control flow across files. Comment-only lines are ignored by the yaYUL assembler, so the code itself is unchanged. Note: since this fork diverges from the upstream archival-fidelity policy, these annotations are intended for this fork's educational use, not for upstreaming.

title: Alarm-trace numbering fix + memory-leak trace + definitions & walkthrough docs
body: Continuation of the Apollo 11 1201/1202 alarm exploration (follows merged [#1](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/1)). ### 1. Fix alarm-trace numbering (split note 7 into 3 locations) The alarm-recording step passed through three distinct labeled locations but was bundled under one `NOTE(ALARM7)`. Split so each has its own ordered number; trace renumbered 12 → 14: - `NOTE(ALARM7)` `BAILOUT1` (catch code) · `NOTE(ALARM8)` `CHKFAIL1` (store code) · `NOTE(ALARM9)` `PROGLARM` (light PROG lamp) · `NOTE(ALARM10)` `WHIMPER` (restart) - downstream renumbered: `START11` `ENEMA`, `START12` queue wipe, `RSTAB13` `5.4SPOT`, `SERV14` `REREADAC` ### 2. New `MEMORY_LEAK` trace (isolates only the job-not-finishing leak) A second, narrower annotation trail so the resource leak can be followed on its own: ```bash grep -rn "MEMORY_LEAK[0-9]" Luminary099/*.agc ``` - `MEMORY_LEAK1` — `SERVICER.agc`: the relentless 2-second re-arm (demand) - `MEMORY_LEAK2` — `SERVICER.agc`: `FINDVAC` allocates a brand-new `SERVICER` every cycle - `MEMORY_LEAK3` — `EXECUTIVE.agc` `VACFOUND`: claim a VAC area - `MEMORY_LEAK4` — `EXECUTIVE.agc` `CORFOUND`: claim a core set - `MEMORY_LEAK5` — `EXECUTIVE.agc` `ENDOFJOB`→`ENDJOB1`: the release (`XCH PRIORITY`) the overrun job never reaches in time ### 3. `definitions.md` A full glossary: core concepts (what **VAC**, core set, job, task, DSKY, CDU, etc. mean), every assembly **instruction** encountered (`CA`, `TS`, `CCS`, `TC`, `INDEX`, `EXTEND`, …) plus assembler directives, and every **hard-coded location/constant** that matters (`CDUT`/`CDUS`, `PRIORITY`, `VACnUSE`, `NO.CORES`, `OCT 1201/1202`, etc.), with number-base notes. ### 4. `walkthrough.md` A jargon-free, high-level overview of exactly what happened: the cast, the five beats (radar theft → clock stays punctual → memory leak → alarm → restart-as-a-feature), why it wasn't a bug, and the fixes. Markdownlint passes (`npm run lint`, 0 errors) — the two new files use `.md` so they're covered by CI. All `.agc` edits are comment-only, so the assembled code is unchanged.

title: Split Apollo 11 alarm investigation into three source tours and ordered guides
body: Reworks the Apollo 11 1201/1202 investigation into **three independent causal trails**, each with its own source markers, explanation document, and Vim quickfix tour. This replaces the combined `apollo_trace.lua`, which mixed multiple concerns. ## Start here `table_of_contents.md` defines the required reading order: 1. `definitions.md` — terminology, AGC instructions/directives, word size, constants, memory locations 2. `radar_problem.md` + `radar_problem.lua` 3. `memory_leak.md` + `memory_leak.lua` 4. `alarm_recovery.md` + `alarm_recovery.lua` Supporting references follow: `walkthrough.md`, `timeline.markdown`, `errorcodes.markdown`, `outline.markdown`. ## Part 1 — Rendezvous-radar time theft (`RADAR_PROBLEM1…4`) Four exact source locations: Channel 12 radar control bits → `RRAUTCHK` (software sees mode but not electrical phase fault) → `RRZEROSB` removes normal zeroing → `CDUT`/`CDUS` hardware counters receive up to 12,800 external requests/s, stealing ~15% CPU. Explicitly distinguishes **rendezvous radar** from the later voice-radio conversation, and states plainly that this cost was **time only — zero words of memory**. ## Part 2 — Unfinished-job resource leak (`MEMORY_LEAK1…9`) Nine exact locations: fixed 2-second re-arm → `T3RUPT` → `READACCS` → fresh `FINDVAC` allocation → `VACFOUND` claim → `CORFOUND` claim → long priority-20 `SERVICER` starts → intended `TCF ENDOFJOB` finish → `ENDJOB1` actual core/VAC release. Now also documents the quantitative answer to "why did losing 15% stop a job from finishing": - duty-cycle table by flight phase (margins of 15% / 13% / ≤10% / <10%) - 90% software demand + 15% theft = 105% of real time - why the shortfall lands entirely on `SERVICER` (lowest priority, "last crack" at CPU time) - per-cycle breakdown: 1.700 s available vs. ~1.800 s needed = ~0.100 s/cycle shortfall - exact memory arithmetic: 12-word core set + 43-word VAC workspace = **55 words (~110 bytes)** held per unfinished copy; pool = 96 + 220 = **316 words**, about 15% of all erasable memory ## Part 3 — Detect, report, restart, recover (`ALARM_RECOVERY1…12`) Twelve exact locations. Steps 1–2 are the alternative 1201/VAC branch; steps 3–4 are the alternative 1202/core-set branch; both join at step 5: `BAILOUT1` → `CHKFAIL1` → `PROGLARM` → `WHIMPER` → `ENEMA` → queue/resource wipe → `5.4SPOT` phase-table rebuild → `REREADAC` continuation. ## Vim usage From repo root: ```vim :luafile radar_problem.lua :luafile memory_leak.lua :luafile alarm_recovery.lua ``` Each quickfix entry points to exactly one source line. Use `:cnext` / `:cprev`. All `.agc` changes are comment-only. Markdown lint passes with 0 errors; all sizes are verified against `ERASABLE_ASSIGNMENTS.agc` and `EXECUTIVE.agc`.

title: exec-tui: interactive AGC Executive simulator — fly the Apollo 11 computer through the 1201/1202 alarms
body: ## What this is A completely new TUI (`exec-tui/`) implementing the wireframe: an interactive, real-time simulation of the LM guidance computer's **Executive** during the powered descent, built for an educational video. - **Top**: how much **free compute** is left, live (plus duty, counter steal, deficit, PROG lamp, FAILREG). - **Left, long lines**: the tasks that need computing — one scrolling execution timeline per job/interrupt (SERVICER, MONITOR, CHARIN, DAP, T4RUPT, RR STEAL, IDLE, …). - **Right, two box columns**: the **8 core sets** and **5 VAC areas** with live ownership. - **Bottom dashes**: interactive controls — `d` descent (2-second READACCS/SERVICER cycles), `l` landing-radar lock, `n` Neil types V16N68 with human cadence, `t` *your* keys become DSKY keystrokes that cost real compute, `r` the rendezvous-radar bug (~15% TLOSS), `p` ping the radar, `6` P64, `a` ATT HOLD. - Time scale: 1000 ms wall = 50 ms AGC (20× slow motion), adjustable. ## Demo video (~5.5 min, includes faked human typing) The full arc: idle → P63 descent → landing-radar lock → Buzz types V16N68 → radar pings → the RR bug steals 15% → pools fill one leaked SERVICER per cycle → **1201 alarm → BAILOUT → restart sheds the monitor** → re-keyed monitor → second alarm → P64 alarm storm (protected load) → **ATT HOLD saves it**. Five alarm/restart events total — same count as the flight. [agc_exec_tui_full_demo_with_typing.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-11caf6d1-ac38-4319-a642-99d354aea41b/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fagc_exec_tui_full_demo_with_typing.mp4) ## Research Every constant is sourced against Luminary 099 in this repo, Don Eyles' AAS 04-064, and the Cherry memo — see `exec-tui/RESEARCH.md`. Notables: - RR bug steals 2 × 6400 × 11.72 µs ≈ **15.0%**, invisible to software (PINC/MINC). - Duty-cycle budget matches Eyles: P63 <85% → LR +~3% → V16N68 monitor +3% → P64 >90%. - Keystrokes fire KEYRUPT → CHARIN at priority 30 (`CHRPRIO OCT 30000`), preempting SERVICER (20). - Equal-priority rescans favor the newest SERVICER, so stubs starve holding core set + VAC — one leaked pair per overloaded cycle, matching the ~6 cycles from V16N68 to the first 1202 in flight. - BAILOUT → FAILREG → PROG lamp → restart: pools wiped, one SERVICER rebuilt, unprotected monitor dropped (P63 self-heals; P64 can't shed, alarms recur; ATT HOLD saves it). ## Tests first Per the repo's development rules: the full suite (15 engine test groups + 6 UI test groups, each with happy *and* unhappy paths) was committed failing before any implementation existed — see history. `go test ./...` and `go vet ./...` are green. ## Docs `exec-tui/ROADMAP.md` (complete design/roadmap), `exec-tui/RESEARCH.md` (sourced numbers), `exec-tui/README.md` (usage + the July 20, 1969 reproduction script). To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

title: Source-validate the alarm timeline and add the descent-replay website spec
body: ## Summary Two pieces of work, both driven by a review of the three primary sources (Robert Wills' *Light Years Ahead* talk, [Cherry's *Exegesis of the 1201 and 1202 Alarms*](https://www.ibiblio.org/apollo/Documents/CherryApollo11Exegesis.pdf), and [Eyles' *Tales From the Lunar Module Guidance Computer*](http://www.klabs.org/history/apollo_11_alarms/eyles_2004/eyles_2004.htm)). ### 1. Validation fixes (what the sources actually say) The programmed data was overwhelmingly correct — alarm codes/counts/times, altitudes, job priorities, the 15% RR ECDU theft math, duty-cycle margins, and pool sizes all match Cherry and Eyles. Five concrete corrections: - **"~40 s from V16N68 to the first 1202" was wrong in three docs** (`memory_leak.md`, `timeline.md`, `errorcodes.markdown`). Flight record: keyed ~102:38:04 (DELTAH callout logged 102:38:06), alarm at 102:38:22 — **~12–18 s**, six to nine guidance cycles. `exec-tui/RESEARCH.md` already used the correct figure; the docs now agree with it and with the ~8–14 s growth diagram in `timeline.md` itself. - **Alarm 2 (102:39:02) was listed *after* Aldrin's 102:39:14 "1668" remark** in the master table — reordered chronologically (the remark reacts to the alarm). - **Throttle down corrected 102:39:35 → 102:39:31** (Eyles, voice transcript). - **Missing keystrokes added**: Aldrin keying **V57** (accept LR updates) and re-keying **V16 N68** (DELTAH → ~900 ft) between alarms 1 and 2, per Eyles; plus the 102:36:55 yaw-around row and a note that the alarm readback was **V05 N09** (Eyles' 2004 paper misprints it as "Verb 90 Noun 50"). - **Pre-existing markdownlint failures fixed** in `definitions.md` (CI was red on every push: heading spacing, double blank line, a merged Job/Task table row). ### 2. `website_spec.md` — descent-replay website implementation spec Implementation-ready spec for the site: night sky + starfield + lunar terrain + LM, driven by the **same `exec-tui/sim` engine** (recorded `flight.json` for static replay, WebSocket bridge for live "fly it yourself" mode). Includes: - **Test plan first** (per repo rules): existing-test inventory with change verdicts, then every new test as an individual item, each with happy and unhappy paths (engine GET clock/snapshots/determinism, redesignation + ROD inputs, bridge protocol, web loaders/playback/DSKY/joystick, Playwright e2e). - **Validated replay dataset**: full event/keystroke script (V37E63E → PRO → V16N68 → V05N09 → V57 → … → touchdown), the five alarms with GET + Cherry PDI offsets + altitudes, trajectory anchors and interpolation rules. - **Time controls**: play/pause, 0.1×–16× rates, exact ±10 ms stepping, +2 s cycle step, scrub bar with event pips, jump-to-event. - **ACA joystick + ROD switch spec**: P64 LPD redesignation (each click queues extra guidance work — measurably deepening the overload), ATT HOLD rate-command, P66 ±1 ft/s clicks. - Architecture, JSON data contracts, milestones M0–M6, risks/open questions (LPD click quanta, sub-second uncertainty, Mode-B trajectory divergence). ## Testing - `npm run lint` — 0 errors (was 3 on master). - `go test ./...` in `exec-tui` and `timeline-tui` — all pass (no Go code changed).

title: Spec update: narrow companion layout, shared-engine TUI link, cog menu, happy-vs-actual walkthrough
body: ## Summary Reworks `website_spec.md` for the two-windows-one-monitor setup (TUI + website on a single 4K display), resolves the spec's M0 research questions from the Luminary 099 source, the ALSJ, and the Apollo Flight Journal, and keeps the spec synced with master (operations & timing audit [#7](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/7), cockpit switch panel [#9](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/9), DSKY component [#10](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/10), compact layout v4 [#11](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/11), DSKY alarm readout + row costs [#12](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/12), lander-lab + 'f' flight recreation [#13](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/13), stars-lab [#14](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/14), LM sprite atlas [#15](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/15), seg-lab [#17](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/17)). ### The website consumes the repo's own assets The lab packages now define the site's art directly, not just by imitation: - **LM sprite**: rasterized from `lander-lab/sprites/lm.json` — the same 4-size × 8-heading atlas the TUI renders (per-cell glyph + xterm-256 color, JSON round-trip pinned by tests); 8 headings give smooth attitude steps across P63/P64/P66. - **DSKY digits**: the repo's `seg-lab/font/SegmentedAlpha.ttf` via `@font-face` (official Unicode 7-seg digit codepoints, 14-seg PUA letters). - **Starfield**: `stars-lab` conventions — four depth-class glyphs (· ˚ * ✦), white/light-blue/faint-red tints (no gold — that's the LM's), **no twinkle** (depth via per-class parallax, the DustRush model), paint-first z-order. - **Scene mechanics**: `lander-lab`'s √-scaled altitude ladder, persistent alarm markers pinned at firing altitudes, plume flicker, touchdown countdown. ### Layout: extremely narrow portrait column Design width **600 px**, hard max **800 px**, min 560 px; design height **2160 px** (full 4K height), collapsible to 1440 px with an explicit zone-collapse order. Zones: clocks → descent scene → DSKY → executive board → hand controls → captions → transport, plus the bottom-right cog. No horizontal scrolling, ever. The web caption feed is the narrative record in companion mode (the TUI dropped its event log). ### Linking the website and the TUI A **Director** (`exec-tui/sim/director.go`) becomes the single writer for engine, clock, scenario, breakpoints, and scripted keystrokes; both frontends speak the same `ControlCommand` vocabulary; `exec-tui --serve :8443` makes the TUI itself the server. **The 'f' historical recreation (#13) is the flight-script driver the spec called for** — `flightPlan()` fires real engine actions at true mission times and the alarms emerge from computation; M2 promotes it whole into the Director. The M0 validation script cross-checks `events.json`/`trajectory.json` against the TUI's `flightPlan()`/`flightPath` tables (current deltas all inside tolerance). The `ui` pause/typing, switch-panel, and flight-plan tests are the frozen refactor contract; `TestServeOffIsInert` keeps the no-server path byte-identical. Controls: DESCENT / DELTAH / RR STEAL switches (typed `V37E63E`, `V16N68E`/`V34E`, RR mode), `.` pause; web transport re-keyed to match; flight-style **V05 N09 alarm readout** on the DSKY; per-job ms row costs from `UsedMs`. ### Cog menu, scenarios, and the exhaustion walkthrough - Bottom-right ⚙ opens: scenario picker (ACTUAL / HAPPY / SANDBOX with the three mission switches), auto-pause toggles, playback, panels, display, connection. Persisted, keyboard-accessible. - **ACTUAL** vs **HAPPY** differ only in the TLOSS input, recorded with shared GET indexing for instant switching; compare mode is a ghost overlay on the executive board. - **Pause-on-alarm** halts on the exact BAILOUT frame; alarm cards report from engine data with running/**sleeping**/stub states distinct (HIGATJOB asleep ~8 s on a VAC at the P64 1201). - **Allocation forensics strip**: per-cycle rows of stub growth, sleepers, and the failing request, click-to-seek; the engine pins the historical alarm-code split (P63 typing → 1202s, P64 VAC hold → 1201). ### M0 research resolved from primary sources LPD click quanta from flight code (`ELEACH` 0.5° / `AZEACH` 2° + the RUPT10 → REDESMON → REDESIG pipeline with P64-only and ATT-HOLD-skip rules); DSKY noun layouts N60–N68 + N09 from `PINBALL_NOUN_TABLES.agc`; pre-PDI sequence timestamped from the AFJ onboard transcript (RR to AUTO TRACK 102:10:16, V37E63E ≈102:10:40, code 500 as flashing V50 N25/00500, V99 N62 at TIG−5); ALSJ facts (RR → SLEW 102:35:38, P64 PRO, LPD series 47°→35°→33°→30°, quantity latch 102:44:31, full 24-row P64/P66 anchor table). Remaining: the inadvertent redesignation's GET and the P63 pitch-profile digitization (scanned external documents). ## Testing - `npm run lint` — 0 errors (14 files). - `go test ./...` — all pass across `exec-tui`, `button-lab`, `dsky-lab`, `lander-lab`, `stars-lab`, `seg-lab`. - Spec test-name inventory cross-checked against the repo: every §1.1 "existing" test exists; every §1.2–1.3 name is planned-new by design.

title: Cockpit switches: reusable toggle component + exec-tui switch panel (DESCENT / DELTAH / RR STEAL)
body: ## What this is 1. **`button-lab/`** — the reusable cockpit **toggle switch** component (`button.NewSwitch`), trimmed to just the winning design after review. Off: lever held down in a ~50%-darker red (xterm 88). Flicked on: lever jumps up lit in two orange tones with a dim glow left in the slot. Raw ANSI 256-color (renders identically in captures/recordings), constant footprint in every state, full happy/unhappy test coverage. The lab program (`go run .`) shows three switches: h/l move, space/enter flick. 2. **exec-tui switch panel** — the big story cards are gone. The controls are now three switches on the bottom panel (imported from `button-lab` via a module `replace`): - **DESCENT** (bottom left) — flicking it keys `V37E 63E` on the DSKY and P63 engages; landing radar acquires on its own - **DELTAH** — Buzz's `V16 N68` ΔH monitor; flicking it off keys `V34E` (the real monitor-terminate verb) - **RR STEAL** (bottom right) — the rendezvous-radar mode switch, instant flip `h`/`l` move between switches, `space` (or enter) flips, pause moved to `.`. body: ## What this is 1. **`lander-lab/`** — the standalone ASCII descent app (continuous zero-rotation fall, live countdown, 1× realtime toggle, 10/10 design-reviewed craft with per-cell materials). 2. **The integration**: press **`f`** in exec-tui and the machine flies the Apollo 11 descent by itself, with the lander descending live in the center gap between the timing graphs and the DSKY (auto-hidden on terminals too narrow to fit it). ## How the recreation works - The **flight plan fires real engine actions at the true mission times** (Cherry's event log): theft active from PDI, radar lock at T+274, Buzz's V16N68 keyed at T+304, **V57E at T+338**, the re-key at T+346, P64 at T+506, ATT HOLD→P66 at T+603. - **The alarms are NOT scripted.** The plan only lights the loads; the 1201/1202s emerge from the engine's own executive arithmetic — and land on the flight's timing (test-pinned: the first alarm must emerge within T+306–335 against the flight's T+316). Tests first: the whole arc (radar lock by T+280, no alarms pre-monitor, first alarm in the T+306–335 window, second by T+380, P64 at T+506, P66 by T+640, ≥3 alarms), f idempotency, replay compression + the raised 16× speed clamp, lander panel presence/absence (no flight, narrow terminals), and engine-alarms-as-markers. title: terminal-fonts: multi-height segment banner font for the TUI
body: ## What A new standalone Go module, **`terminal-fonts`** (package `termfont`), that renders text as multi-height terminal fonts in two cuts — a segment-style **banner font** and true **seven-segment numbers** — following the sibling-lab layout the other modules use. ```go buf, width, err := termfont.Render(height, "APOLLO 11") // banner font buf, width, err := termfont.RenderSeven(height, "12:34 -56") // seven-segment numbers ``` Both share one contract: - Returns a **row-major byte buffer** (exactly `height*width` bytes, space padded, no newlines) plus the **width of each row**, so callers can blit row `r` via `buf[r*width:(r+1)*width]` anywhere inside their own frame data. All output is printable ASCII, so bytes == terminal columns. - **Height 1** is regular terminal printing — the characters pass through untouched. - **Heights 2–5** are ASCII art with hand-authored glyph tables per height. Height 5 is the wide cut: letters, digits, and the seven-segment display cell use 4-column bodies so the tallest size doesn't look thin (naturally narrow glyphs — I, T, 1 — keep their cut). - **Anything outside 1..5** fails with `ErrInvalidHeight`; undrawable runes fail with `ErrUnsupportedRune` (the message names the rune and its index). On error: nil buffer, zero width — never partial output. - `Lines` / `LinesSeven` are the convenience row views. Zero dependencies, pure functions, no ANSI in the buffer. **Banner font** (`Render`/`Lines`, `Charset`): A–Z, 0–9, space, 16 punctuation marks; lowercase folds to uppercase; zero is slashed so it never reads as O. **Seven-segment numbers** (`RenderSeven`/`LinesSeven`, `SevenCharset`): the ten digits plus space and the display marks `. : -`. True seven-segment shapes — straight `_` and `|` segments only, no diagonals, unslashed zero, and all ten digits share one display cell width per height. Letters are rejected at every height, height 1 included — a numeric display shows no alphabet. Height 2 has no top-bar row, so 0 and 7 carry a `~` overline to stay unambiguous. ## Tests first Every feature on this branch was built the same way: the suite written first and committed red (`acc09cc`, `813cdcd`, `184cee5`, `3dba6e0`), then the implementation turned it green (`fa608e8`, `0adc3e1`, `b5907fb`, `6b18681`). Every test carries a happy **and** an unhappy path — height validation, height-1 passthrough, buffer geometry/purity, charset coverage, pinned glyph snapshots (including the wide height-5 cut and its narrow exceptions), straight-segments-only and fixed-cell-width display properties, `Lines`/`LinesSeven`, glyph-table integrity, and the demo layouts. `go test ./...`, `go vet`, `gofmt` all clean. All seven existing modules' suites still pass untouched (the only failure seen, `seg-lab/font`, was a pre-existing missing Python `fontTools` dependency in the VM, green after installing it). ## Demo `go run .` prints the A–Z catalog and the seven-segment digits one through zero at heights 1–5, with the alphabet split A–M / N–Z at heights 4 and 5. `-height` selects one height, `-seven` switches to the seven-segment font, `-text` renders custom text. [A-Z catalog and seven-segment digits at heights 1-5](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a035b0-4410-7b6c-80a9-c4f099e5497f/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fterminal-fonts-abc.png) [Seven-segment one through zero at heights 1-5](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a035b0-4410-7b6c-80a9-c4f099e5497f/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fterminal-fonts-digits.png) [Custom text APOLLO 11 at all heights](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a035b0-4410-7b6c-80a9-c4f099e5497f/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fterminal-fonts-apollo.png) Heights beyond five are rejected: [Height 6 rejected with ErrInvalidHeight](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a035b0-4410-7b6c-80a9-c4f099e5497f/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fterminal-fonts-height6-error.png) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

title: Charm v2 migration + exec-tui launcher menu (screenplay, configurators, legacy sim, all labs)
body: ## Why The scene work (rocket sprite, termfont glyphs, z-indexed layers) needs a cell-based compositor. Charm shipped exactly that in v2 (GA Feb 2026): `lipgloss.NewLayer(content).X(x).Y(y).Z(z)` composed by `lipgloss.NewCompositor(...)` over a cell buffer, plus Bubble Tea's new cell-diffing renderer with synchronized output. The repo was on v1 (Bubble Tea 1.3.10 / Lip Gloss 1.1.0) where none of that exists. This PR moves all Charm-dependent modules to `charm.land/bubbletea/v2 v2.0.9` and `charm.land/lipgloss/v2 v2.0.6` (`terminal-fonts` has no Charm deps and is untouched). Tests were updated first per the repo's test-first workflow, then sources ported until green. One commit per module. The branch also carries `screenplay-lab` (#22, merged into this branch) and latest master (#20, the rocket component — pure sprite code, no porting needed). ## exec-tui is now a launcher Running `exec-tui` no longer boots the sim — it opens a scrollable menu (`j`/`k` or arrows move, `enter` runs, `q` quits) listing every runnable program. When a program exits, the menu returns; launch errors surface on the menu's status line instead of killing the launcher. - The list scrolls: the window slides to keep the cursor visible on short terminals. - `exec-tui/menu` was written tests-first (`menu_test.go`: boot, navigation with wrap, scrolling, selection, status line, module location, catalog consistency — happy and unhappy paths throughout), and the loop was smoke-tested end-to-end in a real pty: menu → legacy sim → back to menu → clean exit. ## New tests - `exec-tui/menu/menu_test.go` — the launcher contract (see above). - `exec-tui/ui/compositor_test.go` — pins the behavior this migration exists to deliver: higher-z layers win at overlaps, offsets place sprites inside a scene, and empty compositors/layers render safely. - `exec-tui/ui/color_test.go` — rewritten for the v2 contract: `ForcedColorProfile()` returns `(colorprofile.ANSI256, true)` when `CLICOLOR_FORCE` is set; `main.go` maps it to `tea.WithColorProfile` (the v1 `lipgloss.SetColorProfile` global is gone in v2). ## Mechanical v1 → v2 changes (all modules) - Imports: `github.com/charmbracelet/{bubbletea,lipgloss}` → `charm.land/{bubbletea,lipgloss}/v2`. - `View() string` → `View() tea.View` with `AltScreen` declared on the view; `tea.WithAltScreen()` / `tea.EnterAltScreen` removed (v2 is declarative). String-asserting tests read `View().Content`. - `tea.KeyMsg{Type, Runes}` → `tea.KeyPressMsg{Code, Text, Mod}`; ctrl combos match `msg.String()` (`"ctrl+c"`, `"ctrl+w"`, …) or `Code`+`Mod`; space's `String()` is now `"space"`. - Editor mouse: `tea.MouseMsg` struct → `tea.MouseClickMsg` with `tea.MouseLeft`; mouse mode declared on the view. - `lipgloss.Color` is now a function returning `color.Color`, so color-typed fields/params switched to `image/color.Color`. ## Behavioral notes worth reviewing - **Styles always render in v2.** v1 stripped ANSI without a TTY, which is why most exec-tui tests ran colorless and a few opted in via `withColor`. That helper is deleted; row-parsing test helpers strip ANSI before matching. Downsampling happens in Bubble Tea's renderer at output time. - **`Width()` is border-box in v2** (includes borders). The two `timeline-tui` boxes now use `Width(width)` for the identical v1 footprint (a test caught the Gantt lane wrapping without this). - **seg-lab space key**: v1 delivered space as a non-rune key so it never typed; the port keeps that as an explicit no-op. - `seg-lab` go directive bumped 1.24.0 → 1.26.3 (v2 requires ≥ 1.25). ## Verification `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` pass in all 9 modules (seg-lab's font test needs Python `fontTools` on the host). The launcher was manually verified in a pty. gofmt-clean except the pre-existing `seg-lab/seg/seg.go` on master, intentionally left untouched.

title: screenplay-lab: scenes, screenplays, and a two-scene premiere (tests first)
body: ## What A new standalone lab that introduces the **screenplay** idea: a screenplay is one or more scenes; a scene is anything that can start, update, render, and stop; `space` cuts to the next scene. The demo bill has two scenes: 1. **arrival** — a drifting starfield; the full zoomed-in craft (size-4, 26×10, W heading) slides in from the right edge with live left-to-right booster fire trailing off its tail, parks at center stage, then bobbles ±1 full cell on a sine with a 10-second period. (Half-cell bobbing would need half-shifted art the atlas doesn't have, so the bobble rides whole cells, as discussed.) 2. **the end** — `THE END` in the height-5 terminal-fonts banner, centered under the same sky. Plus a second adjusting tool in the adjustflame mold: **`cmd/adjuststars`**, the sky tuner — the whole starfield plays behind a panel of eight numbers (a fly **delay** and a **density** for each of the four star layers); `j`/`k` select, `h`/`l` change, and the sky reacts live. It's built as a `screenplay.Scene` on a one-scene bill, so the same lifecycle that runs the premiere runs the tool. **The sky now has the fire's file-config shape.** `stars.SkyConfig` mirrors `fire.HeatConfig`: a JSON file of the eight knobs with `DefaultSky`, `UseSky`/`ActiveSky`/`ResetSky` (the package-active setting), and `LoadSky`/`Save` with sentinel validation. `adjuststars` opens the file (`-config`, default `cmd/adjuststars/stars.json`, committed with stock values like `flame.json`), applies every nudge live, and `s` saves the file and quits. The premiere loads the same file at boot (`-stars`; missing file = stock sky) and its scenes cast `NewTunedStarfield()`, which follows the active sky every frame — **a tuned config just works in any scene**. Verified end to end: tune, save, reboot the premiere → 196 near stars on screen vs 13 stock. Backing it, **`stars.Field` grew a `Density [4]int` knob** (stars per 1000 cells per layer; zero value keeps the stock sky via `DefaultDensity`, floors keep layers alive, a cap stops floods). ## Design Built on the Charm v2 migration (#21) — this PR is **based on that branch** and should land after it. - `Scene` is the generic four-verb interface: `Start()` allocates, `Update(dt)` advances clocks (no render data), `Render(*Screen)` writes cells, `Stop()` deallocates. - `Screen` is the shared render target every scene gets a pointer to: a **Lip Gloss v2 `Canvas`** — one `uv.Cell` of content + style per terminal cell — plus `Resize`/`Resized()` bookkeeping so a terminal change repaints everything. - `Screenplay` owns the frame loop: clears the screen, runs update-then-render on the current scene only, `Next()` stops the old scene before starting the new, `Stop()` ends the run. - `Ensemble` keeps the "scene = cast of sprites" shape: the cast is assembled at `Start`, dropped at `Stop`. - The `screenplay` package speaks lip gloss cells only; the labs' xterm-256 art crosses over in `cast/blit.go`. Everything spaceship-specific stays isolated in `cast/`. - Bubble Tea v2 TUIs with the exec-tui `CLICOLOR_FORCE` → ANSI256 hook so tapes/CI keep their color; one fix riding along wires that same hook into `exec-tui/cmd/adjustflame`, whose runner page recorded as monochrome without it. ## Tests Written first (red suites committed separately), happy and unhappy paths throughout: screen/ensemble/screenplay lifecycle semantics, the blit bridge, ship flight path and flame placement, title and starfield actors, the demo TUI, the `stars.Density` knob, the adjuststars tuner (seeding, live sky reaction, rail clamps, keys), and the config file lifecycle (SkyConfig round-trips, sentinel validation, active-sky swap/reset, tuned starfield following `UseSky`, `Open`/save-and-quit/failed-save flows, the premiere's apply-if-present boot). All nine lab suites pass on the merged base. ## Demo Two-scene premiere (fly-in, full 10-second bob, spacebar cut to THE END): title: stars: evenly spread scatter in a random order — no center stripe, no Gaussian
body: ## Problem Stars looked concentrated at the center of the sky. The scatter was never a normal distribution (it is a splitmix64 hash reduced mod width/height), but three structural issues made it uneven: 1. A deterministic "anchor comb" planted a dust/spark star **every 5 columns across the entire mid row**, while the random scatter skipped that row — a bright stripe at the vertical center. 2. The fixed-seed hash deterministically doubled up single rows at common sizes (row 15 of a 30-row sky drew twice its share). With ~13 stars per row expected, independent draws always produce a ~2x outlier row somewhere. 3. Even with rows fixed, purely hashed columns left holes and clumps inside rows — up to a 64-cell empty stretch on a 128-wide row, with column bands swinging 56–134% of their fair share. ## Fix: stratified in both axes, hashed jitter for the random look Tests first in `stars/distribution_test.go` (happy + unhappy): no row exceeds ~1.5x the average across a matrix of sizes; the middle third of rows and of columns holds roughly a third of the stars (uniform, never normal); every row's largest cyclic gap stays within 3.5x the fair spacing; each quarter of the width holds 15–35% of the stars; and narrow, one-row, and one-column skies stay safe. `catalog` now: - drops the mid-row comb; the four fixed glyph anchors remain, - stratifies **rows**: each layer walks the sky with a golden-ratio stride coprime to the height, - stratifies **columns**: each star owns an evenly spaced stratum of the row its stride assigns it and lands at a hashed offset inside it, with a hashed per-row phase so rows never align into a lattice; sparse layers (under one star per row) roam the whole width; a star stalled by collisions widens its jitter window until it escapes, - stays fully deterministic and pure, as before. The motion tests now read glyph columns straight from `Paint` instead of the rendered grid, so a faster layer crossing a slower one no longer hides the star being tracked. That let the scatter cover the mid row too (it was briefly anchors-only, which read as a faint dark line across the center). ## Result (128×30, `Still`) Before: average 13.6 stars/row, mid row **29** (evenly spaced comb), 64-cell holes inside rows. After: every row holds 12–17; worst in-row hole drops from ~6.4x fair spacing to ~2.8x; width quarters hold 22–27% each. ## Testing - `go test ./...` in `stars-lab` and `screenplay-lab` (cast starfield, adjuststars tuner, premiere): pass. - `gofmt` / `go vet`: clean. - Plain-text renders at several sizes confirm an even, random-looking sky with no center artifacts.

title: One home for the show: components/ + cmd/ in exec-tui, sprite-returning Component lifecycle
body: ## What this does Dissolves `lander-lab`, `stars-lab`, and `screenplay-lab` into `exec-tui`, so one module owns the whole show, and replaces the paint-on-screen `Actor` with a `Component` that returns pixels. ### The new organization ``` exec-tui/ components/ everything a scene puts together sprite/ Sprite = width × height cells (rune + fg/bg); generic, LM art moved out particle/ the particle engine fire/ flame, booster, compass — owns its config.json stars/ the four-layer starfield — owns its config.json lander/ the Apollo LM: DefaultAtlas art, lm.json, the Ship component descent/ the legacy descent-view renderer (sim UI + lander demo) rocket/ the size-4 rocket title/ terminal-fonts banner cards screenplay/ Screenplay → Scene → Component; the lip gloss Screen cmd/ every runnable: premiere, lander, stars, preview demos; the sprite editor; adjustflame + adjuststars tuners ``` - Each component's tuning file lives **beside its code**: `components/fire/config.json` (was `exec-tui/cmd/adjustflame/flame.json`) and `components/stars/config.json` (was `screenplay-lab/cmd/adjuststars/stars.json`). The editor's atlas is `components/lander/lm.json`. - The launcher menu now runs everything the module owns out of its own `cmd/` (found by walking up to `go.mod`); only the genuinely separate labs (dsky, button, timeline) still launch as sibling modules. - The stale checked-in `exec-tui` binary is removed and gitignored. ### The component model ```go type Component interface { Start(width, height int) // allocate everything for a w×h stage Update(dt float64) // advance internal clocks Render() sprite.Sprite // this instant's pixels, stage-sized Stop() // free what Start built; Start may come again } ``` Components never touch the screen. `Ensemble` composites their sprites in cast order — later on top, transparency spares the layer below — starts the cast on the first render (when the stage size is known), and restages on resize. No z-index: each scene decides ordering by how it lines up its cast. The stars are the model citizen for the lifecycle: `Start` scatters and **caches** the catalog (`stars.NewCatalog` — every home laid out once), `Render` flies it by tick, `Stop` deletes the array, and the next `Start` re-scatters. The tuned starfield samples the active sky at `Start`. `Ship` and `Title` moved out of the dissolved `cast` package into `components/lander` and `components/title`; the xterm-256 bridge became `Screen.PutCell` / `Screen.Blit`, with `sprite.Blit` for composing a component's own stage. ### Tests first Every behavior change got failing tests before implementation: config homes beside components, editor open/seed, tuner default paths, launcher catalog + `ModuleRoot`, the Component/Ensemble contract, catalog caching, and the Starfield/Ship/Title lifecycles — happy and unhappy paths throughout. All moved suites pass unchanged in spirit. ### Validation - `go test ./...` in `exec-tui`: 18 packages, all passing - `go build ./...` across `exec-tui` and every remaining sibling module - No `lander-lab` / `stars-lab` / `screenplay-lab` references remain outside historical prose

title: Add rough_outline.markdown + rough_descent_timeline.markdown (descent program map, four-region timeline, core-set/VAC reconciliation)
body: ## Description Two small, tight reference docs distilled from the repo's validated research (`operations_and_timing.md`, `timeline.markdown`, `errorcodes.markdown`, `exec-tui/RESEARCH.md`, `website_spec.md`): - **`rough_outline.markdown`** — every program running while the descent engine burned: kind (job/task/interrupt/counter-steal), interval, CPU cost per 2-second cycle, and which held core sets / VAC areas and for how long; a mapped 2-second cycle; duty-cycle percentages by phase; and the reconciliation of why the flight overflowed **core sets 4 of 5 times (1202)** while a stubs-only simulation structurally produces **1201s** (NOVAC sleepers nibbling the 8-set pool; NOVAC requests can only raise 1202; FINDVAC scans VACs first). - **`rough_descent_timeline.markdown`** — four regions: (1) undocking → PDI (near-idle machine, average-G starts PDI−30 s), (2) the 10% throttle phase (trim-gimbal, not a test; core loop only), (3) P63 full throttle with Aldrin's 1668 (V16N68 keyed ~102:38:04 → the two P63 1202s), (4) P64 with alarms 3–5 including the ~2,000 ft 1202, plus the correction that **P66 never alarmed** (last alarm was 22 s before P66 entry). Numbers use Cherry's canonical PDI offsets (+316/+356/+552/+578/+594) consistent with the existing docs. ## Motivation and Context Requested summary docs validating what programs ran, at what intervals, and at what percent of expectations, across pre-PDI / 10% throttle / P63 / P64 / P66 — and reconciling the sim's 1201 bias against the flight's 1202-dominant record. ## How Has This Been Tested? Docs-only change. `.markdown` files are outside the markdownlint CI glob (`*.md`); content cross-checked against the repo's sourced docs. ## Types of changes - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) ## Checklist: - [x] My code follows the code style of this project. - [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation. - [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly. - [x] I have read the **CONTRIBUTING** document. - [ ] I have added tests to cover my changes. - [ ] All new and existing tests passed.

title: premiere: descent-orbit scene — the moon with the descent path circling it
body: ## What The moon show, built up across this branch: - The premiere gains a **descent orbit** scene between the DSKY dock and THE END — the moon with the lone gold craft circling it, so the show can say *this is where the moon lander was, and why it's flying sideways*. - **The moon screenplay** — a separate, composable two-scene show (`shows/moonshow`, played by `go run ./cmd/moon` / the MOON SCREENPLAY launcher entry): it opens on **just the moon**, space brings a **fast spaceship that streaks in, brakes smoothly onto its orbit, and circles indefinitely**, and space on the last scene **ends the show**. - **No line around the moon** — the craft alone traces the path — and the entry is **velocity-matched**: the streak decelerates into exactly orbital speed, so there's no slow-to-a-crawl-then-speed-up stall at the merge. - **Composable screenplays**: `screenplay.Bill` + `screenplay.Compose(bills...)` add shows' bills together into one big screenplay. - **The moon itself is a component**: `moon.Moon` is the reusable pixelated disc alone; `moon.Orbit` is the lone craft circling it, painted over transparency. - **`AGENTS.md`** (new, repo root): top line — *every change requires a video attached to it if there's any sort of TUI change.* ## Demo The moon screenplay end to end on the current build — just the moon; space; the lander's fast entry braking seamlessly into two clockwise 12-second laps (no line, no stall); space ends the show: [moon_screenplay_no_line_smooth_orbit_entry.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a03c07-fe3a-789b-b310-6fa052a29909/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fmoon_screenplay_no_line_smooth_orbit_entry.mp4) ## The pieces - `components/moon` — two performers sharing one Geometry so any orbit fits any moon: - `Moon` — the pixelated gray disc alone (near-side maria, crater pits, softened limb, speckle grain), a static reusable card; - `Orbit` — the **lone gold craft** (`◆`, mission gold) circling clockwise — eastward over the top — one lap every 12 s, no line drawn; `Arrive()` streaks the craft in fast off the left wing and **brakes velocity-matched onto the orbit** (`ArrivalAt` is the exported path: a quadratic in time-remaining whose end speed equals the orbit's eastward pace). - All circle math runs in half-cell "pixels" so the disc and the orbit read round on a real terminal. - `components/stars` — **delay 0 parks a layer** (strategies, `SkyConfig`, the adjuststars tuner), and `Starfield.Still()` parks a tuned sky outright. Every moon scene plays under a perfectly still sky. - `screenplay` — `Bill` + `Compose`, the composability primitives. - `shows/moonshow` — the moon screenplay's bill: "the moon", then "orbit". - `cmd/moon` — the runner: space cuts, and past the last scene the show ends; `-seconds` for tapes, `-stars` for a tuned sky. ## Tests first Written and committed red before each implementation (see history), happy + unhappy paths throughout: - `screenplay/compose_test.go` — bills add together in order and play across the seam; an empty composition never moves. - `components/moon/moon_test.go` — geometry (wide surface-to-orbit gap, zero-geometry stages); the orbit and arrival paths (on the orbit radius, eastbound over the top, exact merge at `ArriveSeconds`, lap closure, clamps, sentinels, and **no stall at the merge**: the final half-second of the streak covers at least half the orbit's pace while the entry opens faster still); the `Moon` component (disc alone in surface glyphs only, static under updates, lifecycle, nil-safe, tiny stages); the `Orbit` component (**exactly one opaque cell — the gold craft, no line**, update flies it, deterministic, `dt <= 0` holds, clock survives restarts, lifecycle, nil-safe); the arriving orbit (opens empty, streaks in, settles on). - `components/stars` — zero/negative delays park layers; all-zero configs round-trip as still skies; `Still()` keeps tuned densities; the tuner's knobs floor at 0. - `shows/moonshow/bill_test.go` — two scenes in order; scene one bare and perfectly static; **scene two opens rendering exactly like scene one** (nothing rises but the ship), streaks the ship in, orbits on, sky frozen; the composed show walks the bill and then has nothing left. - `cmd/moon/demo_test.go` — opens on 1/2 "the moon"; space cuts to 2/2 "orbit"; space on the last scene issues `tea.Quit`; q/ctrl+c, `-seconds`, window-fill. - `cmd/premiere/demo_test.go` — the four-scene bill, the orbit card's frozen sky and craft-only guards, THE END at 4/4. - `menu/menu_test.go` — the catalog demands the moon entry in the DEMO section. `go test ./...` matches the pre-change baseline: everything green except the two pre-existing, unrelated failures in `components/lander` (atlas mirror test) and `components/rocket` (fire overlap test). title: Alarm-mechanism corrections from primary sources: no typing — the display pipeline (MAKEPLAY / flashing V06N64) is the missing core-set/VAC pressure
body: ## Description Follow-up to #26 (merged). Corrects the alarm-code reconciliation in `rough_outline.markdown` and `rough_descent_timeline.markdown` after a primary-source research pass: Cherry's *Exegesis* (MIT, 4 Aug 1969 — incl. a verbatim OCR of his Table of Jobs and Priorities and event log), the Tillman downlist memo (Grumman, 31 Jul 1969), Eyles AAS 04-064 (both mirrors), Adler's ALSJ Program Alarms note, the Garman oral history, the Wills TNMOC talk, and a full census of every FINDVAC/NOVAC caller in `Luminary099/`. ### What changed - **Retracts the "continuous typing" explanation.** V16N68 is keyed once; `MONREQ` (WAITLIST) respawns the NOVAC `MONDO` job at exactly 1 Hz automatically. Tillman's downlist: both P63 alarms came "after 12 seconds of a monitor verb"; the three P64 alarms occurred "**with no Crew DSKY activity**." No 1969 source attributes any alarm to keystrokes. - **Adds the real mechanism: the display pipeline.** Every guidance pass spawns a display job (Cherry's MAKEPLAY) at `DISPEXIT`: static V06N63/N60 → NOVAC (core set only); early-P64 **flashing V06N64 → SPVAC, sleeping on a core set + VAC until the crew keys PRO** (+568 in Cherry's log — between the 1201 at +554 and the two P64 1202s). HIGATJOB's VAC hold is ≤22 s (not ~8 s). Real MONDO never sleeps (`MONBUSY` → `ENDOFJOB`). - **Corrected job table** to match Cherry's table + the code census (MAKEPLAY row added; MONDO/CHARIN/LRH/HIGATJOB sleep behavior fixed; only SERVICER / flashing-MAKEPLAY / HIGATJOB / P66's RODCOMP ever take VACs; a NOVAC request can only raise 1202). - **Documents the measured sim baseline** for contrast: replaying the `f` flight plan against `exec-tui/sim` yields ten 1201s / zero 1202s, with 6/8 cores + 5/5 VACs held at every failure instant — and names the actual gaps (no MAKEPLAY, invented MONDO sleep, no flashing-display VAC sleeper; the RESEARCH.md typing mechanism is a workaround, not history). - Timeline doc: adds the +568 PRO row that splits the P64 1201/1202 regimes and corrects the 1668 note (typed once per monitor start; the running load, not keystrokes, caused the P63 1202s). Docs only — no engine changes. ## Motivation and Context The sim almost never overflows core sets while the flight overflowed them 4 of 5 times; the previous explanation ("crew typing supplies the 8th core-set holder") was the sim's own workaround presented as history. This PR grounds the reconciliation in the 1969 primary sources and the flight code. ## How Has This Been Tested? Docs-only change; `.markdown` files are outside the markdownlint CI glob. Claims verified against primary-source quotes and instrumented replays of the sim engine (throwaway tests, not committed). ## Types of changes - [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue) - [ ] New feature (non-breaking change which adds functionality) - [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would cause existing functionality to change) ## Checklist: - [x] My code follows the code style of this project. - [ ] My change requires a change to the documentation. - [ ] I have updated the documentation accordingly. - [x] I have read the **CONTRIBUTING** document. - [ ] I have added tests to cover my changes. - [ ] All new and existing tests passed.

body: ## What A second mode for the particle engine plus a new "dust off" effect built on it: the landing kick-up — something drops, dust blows out of the floor to both sides, and half the specks sweep one full cartoon-wind loop before flying on. ## Video Real-time capture of the real terminal (no time compression), walking every state this change touches: the launcher with the two new entries, the DUST OFF demo (mirrored plumes, braille loops, still center gap), and the DUSTOFF CONFIG editor retuning the kick live (count 26→46, loop flipped down and back up). Left- and right-bound flights spin opposite ways so both visually curl the same side. - The straight rule keeps its own update (`advanceStraight`); the swirl rule gets its own (`advanceSwirl`). Each emitted speck carries a `Curl` plan (delay, signed rate, total turn): even deals sweep exactly 2π mid-flight, odd deals curve gently out — half and half. Only the overlap of `[Age, Age+dt]` with the curl window turns, so a loop closes exactly at any frame rate. ### Dust component (`components/dust`) - `PuffConfig` (JSON beside the component) drives two mirrored swirl engines out of a shared floor point: 15° above horizontal leftward and rightward, with a still 8-column gap between the nozzles. - Concentration picks each cell's symbol: `▒` in light gray at heavy counts, `░` in mid gray at strong counts, and the thin fringe wears braille in deep gray — the exact dots computed from where each speck sits inside its cell (2 dot columns × 4 dot rows), so one config value covers every possible braille swirl. - `Cloud` is the screenplay component; it re-reads the active puff every update so the editor retunes it live. ### Tools - `DUSTOFF CONFIG` (`cmd/adjustdust`): the fire/particle-style tuner — 16 knobs (engine numbers, angle, gap, loop side, shade thresholds, the three grays) over the live kick; `s` saves `components/dust/config.json`. - `DUST OFF` (`cmd/dustoff`): the demo scene, two mirrored plumes around the quiet center gap. - Both registered in the launcher menu. ## Tests Written first and committed red before each green commit (see the commit sequence); every test has a happy and an unhappy path. body: ## What The walkthrough's landing scene now kicks dust off the pad twice — two mirrored dust-off animations blowing out of the surface on both sides of the booster bell, one engine climbing leftward and one rightward, both facing upward (15° above horizontal with upward loops): 1. **When the craft starts slowing down** — the moment the booster begins its throttle steps (`LandThrottleLead` before the pad). 2. **When it stops** — at touchdown. title: gunfire: the Doom shotgun muzzle flame — one-shot red-flame particle effect, config, demo, and tuner
body: ## What A one-time particle effect recreating **the red flame that comes out when you fire the Doom shotgun** — built on the particle engine, tests first (committed red, then green), happy + unhappy paths throughout. The blast can be **aimed any which direction** around the full circle. > Scope note: an earlier revision of this branch staged a whole side-view shotgun blast (barrel, seven pellets, gunsmoke). Per feedback, the effect is now the muzzle flame itself — pellets, smoke, and the barrel are gone; the flame is the star. - **`particle` engine** grows the physics a flame needs, plus the trigger: - `Burst()` — one batch on demand; `Period: 0` engines are pure one-time effects. - `Lift` — upward acceleration (hot gas rises) and `Drag` — exponential speed decay (the eruption dies down), frame-rate independent, zero-cost when unset. - **`components/gunfire`** — the `Blast`: two layers from one muzzle. `Fire()` pops a **white-hot core** (concentration ladder: `·` → `*` → `▓` → white `█` on bright yellow) and erupts the **flame** — lifted, dragged tongues painted by density (`░ ▒ ▓ █`) and age (**yellow 226 → orange 208 → red 196 → ember 160 → maroon 124**, the freshest speck colors the cell). Doom's flash is two sprite frames, so a **dimmer second pulse** follows on a 0.11 s fuse at 60% strength. Then the stage is exactly as it began; `Done()` reports the burnt-out flame; re-firing stacks. - **Any direction**: `angleDeg` covers the whole circle (−180…180: 0 right, 90 up, ±180 left, −90 down; the stock aim is straight up like the first-person flash). Lift stays world-up, so sideways and downward shots still curl their tongues skyward — a downward shot pools against the floor and drifts back up. - **`components/gunfire/config.json`** — every variable linked as data (28 knobs): aim angle, muzzle x/y, pulse delay + fraction, the core ladder, and per-layer count / life / speed / spread / nozzle / max-distance / **lift** / **drag**. `UseBlast` applies live. - **`cmd/gunfire`** — the demo: empty dark stage; space (or `f`) fires; **←/h and →/l swing the aim 15° a press with wraparound**, the status line reading the heading out; one free auto-squeeze for tapes; `-seconds` curtain. - **`cmd/adjustgunfire`** — the tuner: three pages (aim / core / flame), `tab` flips, `h/l` `[`/`]` turn knobs live, `f` fires now, auto re-fire keeps the flame burning, `s` saves the component's config. - **Launcher**: `Gunfire` under Scenes, `GUNFIRE CONFIG` under CONFIG. ## Video Real terminal, real time — the menu, then the demo firing the flame straight up, then **swung around the circle with a shot at each heading** (right 0°, straight down −90° pooling on the floor, left −180°, up-left diagonal 135° — the status line reads each aim out), then the tuner cranking the angle knob past the old rail to 180 and firing leftward from the panel, a glance at the core/flame pages, and `s` saving. title: America scene: full-screen flag fades in from black, then the giant eagle crosses

title: msim: a millisecond, instruction-level Executive — both P63 timelines, and the two 1202s for the flight's reasons
body: ## What this is A new simulator, `msim/`, that runs the LGC **100 µs at a time** with one CPU: SERVICER is an array of ~370 interpreter instructions transcribed line-by-line from `Luminary099/` (every entry cites its source line), each worth 1–5 ms, and the machine switches jobs only between instructions — the DANZIG boundary where `INTERPRETER.agc` L74–L82 tests NEWJOB. Interrupts pause an instruction mid-flight losslessly; the waitlist is hardware-punctual; the RR CDU theft sweeps 12.8–15.0% deterministically. Plus **two interfaces** in exec-tui under a new EXECUTIVE menu section, both over the msim machine with the same three switches ([d] DESCENT — the whole P63 chain, [1] 1668 — Buzz's V16N68 monitor, [r] RADAR STEAL — the theft): - **COMMAND SCREEN** (`agctop`) — live, real-time: every process grouped by what it holds (VAC JOBS / CORESET JOBS / NO-PRIORITY OPERATIONS), pool bars, alarm/restart flash. - **GRAPHS** (`agcgraph`) — **a still, never animated**: 2.5 seconds of "here is what the CPU operates with" under the current switches. No header chrome; three lanes (three rows tall each) over a 180-column window, 20-column label gutter, light-gray gridlines every 100 ms, and a **millisecond axis on every other gray line** (0ms … 2400ms) anchored at its gridline; below, a plain-text legend for every job that ran — `DOWNRUPT: 25.0ms total :: wakes up every 20ms and runs for 0.2ms`. Every toggle re-simulates a fresh portrait; with everything off, only the hardware cadences remain (exactly three legend lines). Healthy opening state: descent on, monitor off, steal off. ## Videos (TUI changes — real terminal, real time) **Graphs screen (static portraits with the ms axis)** — the healthy still with idle gaps, full legend and the 0–2400 ms axis; radar steal ON densifying the green band; 1668 ON adding the amber MONDO spikes; the everything-off portrait (empty lanes over the grid, three-line legend, axis intact); back to healthy; out: [agcgraph_static_portraits_with_ms_axis_walkthrough.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a0407d-648f-7ac5-8363-2ecfc1dee3f6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fagcgraph_static_portraits_with_ms_axis_walkthrough.mp4) **Command screen** — menu launch, the three groups live, both radar-steal flips, 1668 keyed through the pool build-up to the red **1202 NO CORE SETS** (cores 8/8), the restart dropping the 1668 switch by itself, descent drain and resume: [agctop_command_screen_realtime_1202_walkthrough.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a0407d-648f-7ac5-8363-2ecfc1dee3f6/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fagctop_command_screen_realtime_1202_walkthrough.mp4) ## The two timelines (committed artifacts) - [`msim/timelines/p63-baseline.md`](msim/timelines/p63-baseline.md) — P63 radar-locked, RR bug stealing, nobody touches the DSKY: 100 s clean on the ~98% knife edge. - [`msim/timelines/p63-monitor-1668.md`](msim/timelines/p63-monitor-1668.md) — Aldrin's V16N68 at the flight offsets: **1202 at ENTR+10.0 s (cores 8/8, VACs 4/5)**, restart, re-key, **1202 at ENTR+11.0 s**, the six-second third use clean. No 1201 anywhere in P63. ## What the code-truth turned up - **The leak is a word-order effect.** `VACFOUND` stores the VAC-area address into the PRIORITY word's low nine bits (`EXECUTIVE.agc` L170–L174), and SETLOC/EJ1 compare full words — the newest SERVICER copy preempts and wins every scan; stubs park at ~95% complete (Eyles' "uncompleted stubs"). EJ1's ones'-complement minus-zero tie keeps the earlier find. - **The swing factor is the blocked display.** With the monitor owning the DSKY, a completing pass's V06N63 display job sleeps holding its core set (ENDIDLE/NVSBWAIT) until the next pass wakes-and-kills it. - **The system is bistable.** The keying cycle completes (planting the blocked display); the next cycle misses; the preemption cascade caps every copy below its own cost until the restart flushes it. Key → ten seconds → 1202 → restart → re-key → again. Model, calibration anchors, load table, flight-anchor scoreboard, source tensions, deviations: [`msim/RESEARCH.md`](msim/RESEARCH.md). Two independent validation subagents audited the branch (source fidelity: nine checks PASS; mechanical integrity: seven checks PASS; their punch list is landed). ## Tests first Every feature red-committed then greened: 5406d5f→e1a14d6 (engine), 19bbc6b→7165ae1 (100 µs tick), 788cdce→43b38c9 (tie-break), f798012→296c828 (command screen), 336bc0f→d2395af (streaming graphs), 1870562→b69975e (the static 2.5 s portraits + per-name busy ledger), the descent-off chain-cancel, and the ms-axis. Every group covers a happy and an unhappy path. Pre-existing failures in `components/rocket` and `components/lander` reproduce on the clean tree and are unrelated. title: Moonwalk scene: tunable crate climb, ball-tip pole grab, rising flag, pan to the rover

title: Screenplay: how memory-cycle stealing exactly works
body: ## What Adds `screenplay_memory_cycle_stealing.markdown` next to the other screenplay docs. The existing documents state the theft as a fact ("those requests stole processor memory cycles… invisibly") but never open up the machinery. This file answers, at gate level, the questions the rest of the repo assumes: - What "stealing a memory cycle" physically is: the 12-time-pulse MCT as the machine's only unit of execution, with no CPU/memory split to hide in. - How the computer "knew" to yield a cycle: it didn't — a request flip-flop in the Counter Priority Control remembers each radar pulse until the free end-of-every-cycle test at T12 finds it. - How the CPU "switched" for exactly one cycle: the INKL signal freezes the sequence generator's SQ/state decoders mid-instruction, one hardwired `PCDU`/`MCDU` cycle does the read-±1-write, and the frozen instruction resumes from mid-flight. Back-to-back service when both CDUT and CDUS are pending. - Why no software could ever observe it, why the design was rational (the machine's own clocks are PINC'ed counters), and the 12,800 × 11.72 µs = 15% arithmetic restated at cycle level. - A "common misreadings" table (not a write request, not an interrupt, not a list walk, resumes mid-instruction, costs time not memory). House style matched: source-linked footnotes to Cherry's exegesis, the AGC Information Series hardware manuals (paragraph-numbered), R-393 (Hopkins/Alonso/Blair-Smith 1963), and the flight code in this repo. One sourcing nuance is documented in the footnotes: the gate-level documents (AGCIS 5, R-393) show insertion at any memory-cycle boundary — i.e. mid-instruction — while higher-level summaries loosely say "between instructions"; the AGCIS 8 priority-control issue describes the Block I counter address map, so the doc uses the Block II map from AGCIS 30 (counters 0024–0060, CDUT/CDUS at 0035/0036). Cross-links added from `screenplay_outline.markdown`, `screenplay_descent_timeline.markdown`, `table_of_contents.md` (supporting reading), and `radar_problem.md` (the "not an instruction, not an interrupt" paragraph). ## Process notes - Documentation only: no TUI change, so no video is required per `AGENTS.md`. - No code, so the tests-first rule has nothing to attach to — the root markdown docs have no test harness.

title: Shotgun: no vertical stretch, sights always up, the gun owns its trigger — and the sprite critiqued to 10/10
body: ## The fixes Three shotgun bugs plus an art overhaul, all visible in the viewer and the America scene's talon guns: 1. **The gun was WAY too long upright.** Frames were rotated in cell space and then row-doubled into full-block cells, so anything vertical rendered stretched 2x. The spin now happens in square-pixel space (rows doubled *before* rotation, frames compiled through half-blocks), so the gun keeps its on-screen length on every heading. 2. **W, NW and SW hung upside down.** The left half of the compass was a pure in-plane spin. It now mirrors the right half, so the sights always face up. 3. **Firing was not tied to the shotgun component.** `Gun.Fire` overwrote the package-global gunfire config, so guns clobbered each other and callers couldn't control cadence. Now `gunfire.Blast.Use` pins a blast to its own tune (unpinned blasts still follow the global, so the tuner keeps working), `Gun.Start` pins the shipped config onto the gun's own blast, `Fire()` is exactly one shot per call, and the new `FireFrom(left, top)` is the same one-shot trigger for a gun a scene mounts anywhere. 4. **The sprite itself was redrawn under two harsh pixel-art critics** (a Grok agent and a Sol agent scoring 0–10 each round) across ten critique rounds, from 3/10+3/10 to a simultaneous **10/10 + 10/10**: a real pump gun now — magazine-tube band under a bright barrel, warm-wood fore-end with a ring rib, boxed receiver with ejection port and stepped rear sight, comb/belly/recoil-pad stock, guard-steel trigger loop with air around a gold trigger, dark muzzle cap with the brass bead inboard. The two 45° frames are authored: the same nearest-neighbor projection with its one-pixel wounds dressed by hand, pinned by a new unit test — every heading carries exactly the cardinal brass mass (2x2 bead + 2x2 trigger) and no heading strands a gold crumb. ## Merged with master (Skies scene) Master's [#54](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/54)/[#55](https://github.com/ThePrimeagen/Apollo-11/pull/55) extracted the america gunner into `components/armed` (shared with the new Skies scene) while this branch rewired that code to `FireFrom`. One semantic conflict: the Skies test detected the mounted gun by gold ink spread across the weapon, but the critiqued art pins brass to two tight 2x2 masses by design; the detector now reads the gun's own metals (receiver 245, tube 243, guard 240, pump wood 130, brass 178 — none worn by the eagle, clouds, or sky), and the re-aim assertion measures the turn against the same gun aimed east. title: Graphs screen: one SERVICER cycle against a hard white 2 s line — per-process lanes and the P64 switch
body: # The single-cycle portrait The graphs screen (`exec-tui/agcgraph`) still freezes 2.5 s of machine time, but the SERVICER is now entered exactly **once** — the only process that does not repeat. Every other timer (READACCS, the LR gates, R10/R11, MONREQ, DAP/T4RUPT/DOWNRUPT) keeps firing through the whole window, so the servicer's bar IS its completion time, laid against a **hard white line at the 2.00 s guidance boundary** — and every cell of the pass that lands **past the line renders RED**: the coming overflow, visible at a glance. Every process that consumed CPU gets its own labeled row — when it ran and how much — grouped the way the Executive sees memory, plus the thing that is not software at all: ``` VAC JOBS SERVICER · (P64: MAKEPLAY, HIGATJOB) CORESET JOBS MAKEPLAY · LRHJOB · LRVJOB · MONDO · CHARIN · 1/GYRO NO-PRIORITY OPS READACCS · R10,R11 · LRHTASK · LRVTASK · HIGATASK · MONREQ · DAP · T4RUPT · DOWNRUPT COUNTER THEFT RR CDU — the steal itself, ~15% of every millisecond, time only, zero memory ``` ## The story the switches tell — calibrated to the screenplay's own arithmetic The outline's load table and `operations_and_timing.md`'s overload sanity check ("deficit ~0.05–0.10 s per cycle") pin the beats: | Switches | single pass ends | | | :--- | :--- | :--- | | `[d] DESCENT` | ~1.61 s | fits with margin — all green | | `+ [r] RADAR STEAL` | ~1.94 s | the knife edge — fits; the purple RR CDU ribbon appears | | `+ [1] 1668` | **~2.10 s (+5.0%)** | **the documented ~105% — red tail past the line** | | `+ [p] P64` (drops 1668) | **~2.14 s (+6.9%)** | **canon "> 105%" — a longer red tail, no monitor needed** | Getting the 1668 case to the documented deficit meant moving `MondoCost` from the floor of its documented 30–60 ms envelope to the middle (50 ms). The flight anchors hold there — two 1202s at ENTR+10 s/+9 s (memo: ~10–12 s), third short keying clean, baseline untouched — while the envelope's top (60 ms) is excluded for cause: it flips the first alarm to a **1201**, a code the flight never threw in P63. `[p] P64` is the approach phase's own set of jobs — the REDESIG landing-site perturbation equations spliced into every pass (LLGE L335–L408, ~132 ms), HIGATJOB parked on its VAC through the antenna slew (SERVICER.agc L740–L755, L1657–L1679), and the flashing V06N64 display holding core + VAC awaiting PRO. **1668 and P64 are mutually exclusive both ways** — they cannot share the DSKY. One naming note: the request said "P66", but the repo's own timeline (`screenplay_descent_timeline.markdown`) pins the no-monitor overload and the ~2,000 ft alarm to **P64** ("**Still P64, not P66**" — P66 *reduced* load and had zero alarms), so the switch carries the honest label. ## msim underneath - `Sample.ByName` — per-millisecond CPU attribution by consumer, the data behind the per-process lanes. - `Live.SetServicerOneShot` — only the run's first READACCS enters a SERVICER; the lattice keeps firing. - `Live.SetApproach` + `ServicerScript(P64Approach)` + `higatSpec`/`StartHigate` — the P64 machine. - `Engine.SetTheftPhaseMS` — the sweep's phase is the documented free parameter (RESEARCH.md); the portrait rides `TheftPeakPhaseMS`, the "worst 2 s window" (~14.8%), where the flight scenarios keep their floor dwell. The monitor, when keyed, is up at the window's open on the flight's `.985` ENTR phase — its second refresh straddling the white line. - `MondoCost` 30 → 50 ms (mid-envelope; see above) with the RESEARCH.md calibration notes updated. The flight scenarios and their calibrated 1202 timeline stay green throughout (full msim suite). ## Tests Written first and committed red, then made green — every test carries a happy and an unhappy path: - msim: `TestSampleByNameAttribution`/`Idle`, `TestTheftPhaseShiftsTheSweep`, `TestServicerScriptP64ApproachRedesignation`, `TestLiveServicerOneShot`, `TestLiveApproachP64` (red b66b087 → green 01b6381) - agcgraph: `TestSingleServicerCycle`, `TestPerJobRowsGrouped`, `TestHardWhiteLineAtTwoSeconds`, `TestApproachSwitchP64`, `TestMonitor1668AndP64MutuallyExclusive`, `TestServicerBoundaryCrossings`, plus the reworked geometry/legend/toggle tests (red b66b087 → green 01b6381) - the red overrun: `TestServicerOverrunTailTurnsRed` (red cfd2e26 → green 2ae61b0) - the documented deficit + the theft lane: `TestServicerBoundaryCrossings` tightened to the 50–100 ms deficit band, MONDO's 50 ms legend, and `TestCounterTheftLane` (red c73ee9d → green cbaea27) Pre-existing on master, unrelated and untouched: `components/rocket` fails consistently (footpad glyph) and `components/shotgun` `TestEightHeadings` flakes occasionally. ## The video Real-time recording of the real terminal, walking every state: the healthy portrait, everything-off, the radar knife edge with the purple RR CDU theft ribbon appearing, the 1668 crossing ending near 2100 ms with the **red tail past the white line**, the P64 crossing with the longer red tail, both mutual-exclusion flips, and the steal-off retreat where the ribbon and every red cell vanish. title: Core Set scene: nine live knobs, and the survivor lands before the words arrive
body: ## What Tests-first, red commit then green (35059a9 → 592fdb9), plus the stock `config.json` the other scenes also ship (06ec896). ### The reported glitch — validated, then fixed The move act's final frame really did move the box once more, exactly as reported. Frame-by-frame before the fix (100×30 stage): the CORE SET box rests at `(41,3)` through the glide's tail, then hops to `(42,2)` **on the very frame the first word MPAC appears**. The PRIORITY word had the same defect at the zoom→bits flip: `(48,7)` → `(47,8)` on the frame the bit row arrives. Root cause: the glide interpolated with `int()` truncation, so the traveler never quite reached its destination inside its own act — the next act painted it at the exact target, one cell away, in the same frame its content appeared. Two-part fix in `scenes/coreset`: - **`glide()` rounds instead of truncating**, so the box (and PRIO) land exactly on their parking spots while their own act still runs. - **A new settle beat** (`settle`, stock 0.6 s) rests the parked box after the landing and before the first word — first the transition, then the core set's layout. Same contract on the zoom: PRIO is parked on its seat before the bits break open. ### The knobs Every timing of the lesson is now a live knob on `scenes/coreset/config.go`, tuned the way America tunes: | knob | stock | what it drives | |---|---|---| | unit hold | 4.000s | how long the full memory unit holds | | fade beat | 0.220s | the stagger between one box's dissolve and the next | | dissolve | 0.400s | one box's full shade-ramp burn | | move | 1.500s | the survivor's glide to the top center | | settle | 0.600s | the rest after landing, before the first word (new) | | word beat | 0.350s | one word of the twelve-word bar | | word hold | 3.000s | the finished anatomy on stage | | zoom fade | 0.250s | everything else burning away while PRIO holds | | zoom glide | 1.150s | PRIO's ride to center stage | 50 ms steps rounded to the millisecond; floors under the two glides (each divides its clock); `Validate` refuses NaN/negative knobs; JSON save/load next to the scene (missing keys keep stock, corrupt files are loud); `Active`/`Use`/`Reset` so `New` plays the saved tune. The act boundaries became derived clock marks on the config. title: Core Sets Two: the scan scene — the pickup, the job roster, EJSCAN as code, and the full-word compares where the newest copy always wins
body: ## What A second Core Set scene, `Core Sets Two`, that picks up exactly where the Core Set breakdown left off and teaches how the Executive picks the next job — ending on why a duplicated job's newest copy always wins the scan (the engine of the 1202 leak). Six acts on one director clock (`scenes/coreset2`): 1. **The pickup** — opens on *exactly* the frame scene one held at its cut (row for row, ink for ink): the PRIORITY word broken into six priority bits over nine VAC-address bits, OCT 20400, both field labels, the caption. 2. **The roster** — the word burns away while six real jobs land one per beat, each in its own ink with its own priority: SELFCHK·1, SERVICER·20, 1/GYRO·21, MONITOR·26, CHARIN·30, RR READ·32. 3. **The sweep** — the roster dissolves to an empty stage: one CPU, something must pick. 4. **The code** — the EJSCAN loop revealed one line per beat, created by showing it: loop the core sets, read each PRIORITY word, keep the highest — sourced comments from `EXECUTIVE.agc` (EJSCAN L437+, EJ1 L492–L499, CHANJOB L251+), the two bit fields tinted in scene one's inks. 5. **Scan one** — five core sets redraw with the full word math beside each box (`20 + 400 = 20400`; the NOVAC jobs carry a dim `000` — their low nine bits stay empty). The scan speaks every comparison beat by beat, a cursor on the examined set and `◀ best` riding the leader, until the **third box down** — RR READ at 32000 — wears `◀ SELECTED`. 6. **Scan two, the redo** — the duplicated job: three SERVICER copies, all PRIO 20, climbing the real VAC-area addresses 400, 454, 530. Every equal-priority compare falls to the higher VAC address (`PRIO 20 = 20 · VAC 454 > 400 · the newer copy leads`), the newest copy is SELECTED, the free set is skipped (`PRIORITY -0`), and the passed-over copies are tagged `stub — never finishes`. The scene holds on the lesson. `Steps()` is EJSCAN as a pure function — seed, greater, lesser, equal-priority, the EJ1 tie that keeps the earlier find, the skip, and the all-free pool that idles (DUMMYJOB) — so the algorithm itself is unit-tested and the stage just replays it. ## Wiring - `cmd/coreset2` — standalone runner: space/p/enter replays, `-seconds` for tapes, q quits. - Launcher lists **Core Sets Two** under Scenes right after Core Set (Liftoff and Bobble follow the pair); the viewer lists **SCAN** between BREAKDOWN and LIFTOFF, with `e` opening `./cmd/coreset2`. - `scenes/coreset` — the bits painting is extracted to the exported `coreset.PaintBits` so both scenes share one frame (scene one's behavior unchanged; its tests untouched and green). ## Merge with master Master moved under the PR (#60, #61, #63, #64). Merged back cleanly: scene one's timings are now the nine live knobs of #61, so the pickup test asks the show's own `Cfg` for `BitsStart()`; the `PaintBits` extraction and the config rewrite compose without behavior change, and the pickup frame still matches row for row. The liftoff shelving test now anchors on the core-set pair's tail (Core Set, Core Sets Two, then Liftoff, Bobble), and the viewer's SCAN entry carries its path through the new tuner-path assertion. ## Tests Written first and committed red (both new packages failing to build, menu and viewer failing their new assertions), then made green. Happy and unhappy paths throughout: the exact-frame pickup, beat timing of every act, word-math inks, marker rows, stub tags, the hold, resize/replay/nil-screen lifecycle, and the runner's house rules. Note: `components/lander` (`TestEightHeadings`) and `components/rocket` (`TestView`) fail at the base commit before this change — pre-existing, untouched here. ## Video Real-time recording of the merged branch (constant 30 fps capture, no interior edits), walking every state this change touches: the launcher with Core Set and Core Sets Two adjacent, scene one (with its new knob panel) playing to the held bits frame, Core Sets Two picking up that exact frame and playing all six acts — the third-box `◀ SELECTED` in scan one, the newest-copy `◀ SELECTED` with red `stub — never finishes` tags in scan two — the space-bar replay, and the viewer's SCAN entry (three `p` steps past BOBBLE and LIFTOFF).
