title: Interpreter scene: the real SERVICER code scrolling behind a Rose Pine vignette, every chunk ending in its own look for the DANZIG check
body: ## What Two reusable components and a scene composed from them. **`components/code`** just displays code. You hand it lines and the language they're written in — the coloring is private to the component, keyed by language (`agc` for the listing's label/opcode/operand columns, `pseudo` for the danzig dialect; an unknown language stays plain text instead of coloring weirdly). Tabs expand on the listing's 8-column grid, an optional gutter numbers non-empty lines in five-digit octal, and **marks** are the highlighting: the caller says which span of which line to highlight and in what color, and the mark wins over the syntax ink. `Dim` is the vignette ramp: level 0 bright, three deepening rungs per hue, nothing paints past three. The card never moves itself. **`components/scrollcode`** is the moving part. Give it many code cards, flag which are stops, and it stacks them into one column, parks the spotlit card on the anchor, hangs the vignette on **both sides** (bright → dim → faint → barely-there → gone), rests `hold` seconds per stop, glides `glide` seconds on an eased camera that lands exactly before the hold begins, and holds forever on the last stop. `Next()` cuts a rest short for callers driving it by hand. **`scenes/interpreter`** only chooses what to show — and it's the real thing: **MUNRVG**, the average-G integration SERVICER ran every 2 s of the powered descent, **verbatim and consecutive from `Luminary099/SERVICER.agc` (TC INTPRET through RVQ)** — a test literally diffs the on-screen run against the flight source. The DOT altitude-rate block scrolls past unfocused between the last two stops, and **three more real chunks (through MUNGRAV to RVQ) fade out below the final stop** so the tail is more than an EXIT. | stop | real code | the DANZIG check as | |---|---|---| | 1/5 | `VLOAD VXSC` — the ΔV load | the real assembly — `CCS NEWJOB` / `TCF CHANG2`, **verbatim INTERPRETER.agc** | | 2/5 | `PDDL DDV` — the guidance push | pseudocode — `IF NEWJOB != 0: SWAP CORES[0], CORES[NEWJOB]` | | 3/5 | `STCALL R1S` — position out | a fork diagram | | 4/5 | `STORE V1S` — velocity out | a weighing of PRIORITY words | | 5/5 | `VXV VSL2` — **the V×V itself** | a rubber stamp — `NEWJOB = 0 ✓ CARRY ON` | Every `NEWJOB` in the checks wears a love-ink mark; the `VXV` op wears gold — both through the code component's mark API. ## Video Real terminal, real time, in color this time (`CLICOLOR_FORCE` keeps the 256-color profile alive under tmux): the launcher, all five stops with the graded fades running out both sides, the pink NEWJOB and gold VXV marks, the knobs nudged live, a replay, and the INTERPRETER entry inside the Component Viewer: [interpreter_servicer_scroll_rose_pine_color_walkthrough.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a04885-6cd9-7464-b7d9-4d28591736ee/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Finterpreter_servicer_scroll_rose_pine_color_walkthrough.mp4) ## Tests first (red → green) - `34b74db` / `12db834` — the original scene, red then green. - `df13ab1` — red: the component split (code display/coloring/gutter/marks/Dim; scrollcode stacking/vignette/clock/Next) and the real-source legitimacy tests (verbatim + consecutive against SERVICER.agc and INTERPRETER.agc). - `4057d6a` — green: both components land, the scene composes them. title: Slim code scenes: one comment per block, one DANZIG call — and the function walked in Check Priority, Core Sets Two, and Alarms
body: ## What The code experiment slims down, and the check grows into real walkable code across three scenes. **`scenes/interpreter` — the reduced instruction set.** Every spotlit block now reads at a glance: ONE plain comment on top that just says what the block does (`# LOAD THE VELOCITY CHANGE MEASURED THIS CYCLE`, `# UPDATE THE POSITION AND CALL GRAVITY`, …), the bare MUNRVG ops (still verbatim SERVICER — inline comments stripped, still one consecutive run from `TC INTPRET` through `RVQ`, tests diff it against the flight file), and the whole DANZIG construction as literally one pseudo call: ``` check_for_higher_priority_jobs() # DANZIG ``` The five dresses (assembly / pseudocode / fork / weighing / stamp) are gone. ``` # LOAD THE VELOCITY CHANGE MEASURED THIS CYCLE MUNRVG VLOAD VXSC DELV KPIP2 PUSH VAD GDT/2 check_for_higher_priority_jobs() # DANZIG ``` [interpreter_plain_comments_no_narration_walkthrough.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-01a0494f-6e91-75d8-8e47-5e4771009db1/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Finterpreter_plain_comments_no_narration_walkthrough.mp4) **`scenes/checkprio` (new) — the very simple priority check function.** Where the call points, more code: the C-style function revealed line by line, then walked by a gold cursor with a caption per step — ```c check_for_higher_priority_jobs() { old = -0 for (i = 0; i < 8; i++) { new = core_sets[i].data[11] if (new > old) { old = new winner = i } } run(core_sets[winner]) } ``` `data[11]` is the twelfth word of the core set — the PRIORITY register. New against old; the highest priority wins. **`scenes/coreset2` — mixed together with the components.** The scan acts now carry the SAME function (imported from `checkprio`; a test pins the two scenes line-for-line identical) on the right half of the stage — it reveals there and never burns away. Every compare beat walks the code: the `winner = i` line when a set takes the lead, the `if (new > old)` line when the compare says no, the read line when a free set turns up `-0`, and `run(core_sets[winner])` once the box is SELECTED — so you watch it select the newest SERVICER copy in scan two. **`scenes/alarms` (new) — select the next core set or throw.** Two C-ish functions, walked to both famous codes: ```c find_free_core_set() find_free_vac_area() { { for (i = 0; i < 8; i++) for (i = 0; i < 5; i++) { { in_use = core_sets[i].data[11] in_use = vac_areas[i].data[0] if (in_use != -0) if (in_use == 0) continue continue return i return i } } throw new error(1202) throw new error(1201) } } ``` Each function plays a happy pass (a free slot found, its index returned) and the full-pool pass — the loop falls off its end, the throw line burns red under a `PROG ALARM` chip. The scene rests naming both codes. Runners (`cmd/checkprio`, `cmd/alarms`), menu shelf entries right after the Interpreter, viewer catalog items, and `return`/`throw` joining the pseudo dialect's keywords. ## Merge with master Master's Shooting Star claimed the same shelf slot ("right after Interpreter"). title: 05. Main: every scene in one screenplay, inside a full editor
body: ## What **05. Main** is the screenplay that puts everything together: its bill is every numbered show's bill added together — 01. Moon Orbit, 02. Walkthrough, 03. Mario, 04. Inverse Walkthrough — thirteen scenes, and it runs inside **`director`**, the screenplay editor, wearing **MAIN's own numbers**. ### The editor - **Browsing is the quiet face**: the marquee, one **hold** row — how many seconds the scene lasts in play mode before the cut — trimmed directly with `h`/`l`, and the help line. **`ctrl+n`/`ctrl+p`** (or plain `n`/`p`) scroll the scenes both ways; the screenplay grew `Prev()` and `Rewind()` for it. - **`e` edits the scene**: the **MAIN CONFIG** panel opens over the scene now playing — the hold first, then **every one of the scene's own knobs** — `j`/`k` pick a row, `h`/`l` turn it, `e`/`esc` hand the quiet face back. The panel wears the MAIN CONFIG name so it never reads like the scene's standalone tuner. - **MAIN owns its own set of configs**: `s` writes **one file**, `shows/mainshow/config.json` — every scene in bill order with its hold and its knobs in the scene's own JSON shape — and **never** touches a scene package's `config.json` or its `Active`. Tuning MAIN never retunes a scene launched by itself; at boot the saved knobs are laid back onto each scene instance (a blob that doesn't fit is ignored with a word on the status line). Saving from a moonwalk beat syncs its sibling beats (one performance); the two bobble entries keep the bill's word on the engine. - **Every scene has its editable properties now**: the walkthrough's inline ensembles grew tunable faces — the **orbit** (arrive + lap, via a new per-instance `moon.Orbit.Pace`), the **close-up** (fly-in, via a new per-instance `lander.Ship.FlyIn`, driving the sky and hull on one clock), and the **fire** (the brake's depth and window). They join fall (1), landing (24), the moonwalk beats (11), liftoff (9), and the bobbles (3). The moon and the pause genuinely hold still — their one property is the hold, and their panel says so honestly. - **No knob is ever clamped**: zero and negative holds cut at once; nudges below zero stand. - **`space` plays** the show through on the holds; **`f` premieres fullscreen from the top** and hands the chrome back at the end; `r` replays the scene; `q` quits. ## Video Recorded from the real terminal, in real time (174 s, desktop clock visible advancing): browse-face hold trimming and save, `ctrl+n`/`ctrl+p` scrolling, the MAIN CONFIG panels for the orbit (arrive turned 2.5 → 1.0, replayed visibly faster), the close-up (fly-in 4 → 2, ditto), the fire, the fall, and the landing's full 25-row board, then play mode cutting itself through the landing's 1202s, and the fullscreen premiere playing all thirteen scenes — the edited paces visibly live — before the chrome returns on its own. title: QEMU client: a typed object and exported functions — no classes
body: ## What The QEMU client lands as a plain typed object plus exported functions — no class — and AGENTS.md now carries the law: **no classes**. State is a nicely typed object made by a small constructor function; behavior is exported functions that take that object. - `newQemu()` — makes the typed `Qemu` object: `diskPath`, `proc`, `qmp`, all `undefined` until the functions below define them. - `assert(value, message)` — validates a truthy or throws the message. - `newDisk(vm, path, size)` — asserts `diskPath` is still undefined, creates the qcow2 with `qemu-img`, and defines it. - `start(vm)` — asserts the disk, boots `qemu-system-x86_64`, and sets the live process and QMP socket on the object. - `screendump(vm, path)` — asserts the VM started, then dumps the screen over QMP. - `stop(vm)` — asserts the VM started, ends the process, clears it off the object. The QMP plumbing that wires a command to the response that answers it (the screen dump getting the screen dump response) is module-private. ## Tests None ship with the client, per the operator: the client gets tested a different way. The suite that drove the red → green build (and a later CLI-free rework) was removed at the operator's instruction; the history keeps the record. ## Sol pass A sole Sol subagent swept the module to simplify, remove redundant guardrails, and keep it human maintainable. ## No video No TUI is touched — this is a library module plus a rulebook line, so no recording is attached.
